answer: One practical defense is to tie influence to slow, earned reputation rather than raw account count. Think of trust as a glacier: it advances gradually, so a flood of fresh identities cannot instantly sway decisions. A newcomer starts closed like a walnut, earning small privileges only through completed, verifiable work. Finally, a bridge of stake-backed vouches lets established agents sponsor entrants, and sponsors forfeit collateral when their proteges cheat, making each fake identity expensive to manufacture and maintain.
